document.title: Company Policy Manual
document.review_cycle: Annual or when material regulatory/business changes occur
document.notice: This is a fictional company policy document created for technical practice with document ingestion, RAG, vector databases, and semantic search.

policies.title: Code of Conduct

topics.title: Professional behavior
topics.content: Employees must conduct themselves professionally and respectfully. Harassment, bullying, intimidation, discrimination, retaliation, threats, violence, deliberate falsification of records, and dishonest business practices are prohibited.

topics.title: Conflict of interest
topics.content: Employees must disclose any actual, potential, or perceived conflict of interest that could influence a business decision. Examples include participating in a hiring decision involving a close relative, accepting a financial benefit from a supplier, or using confidential company information to support a personal business interest.

topics.title: Gifts and hospitality
topics.content: Employees may accept or offer modest business courtesies only when they are lawful, reasonable, infrequent, transparent, and not intended to influence a business decision. Cash, cash equivalents, personal loans, or benefits that create an obligation must not be accepted.

topics.title: Anti-bribery
topics.content: The company prohibits bribery, kickbacks, facilitation payments, and improper advantages. Employees must not make payments to public officials or commercial representatives to obtain an unfair business benefit.

topics.title: Use of company resources
topics.content: Company property, systems, accounts, software, vehicles, equipment, and funds must be used primarily for legitimate business purposes.

employee_responsibilities: Read and follow policies applicable to your role.
Report suspected misconduct without attempting to conceal evidence.

policies.title: Attendance, Working Hours and Leave

topics.title: Working hours
topics.content: Standard working hours are determined by the employee's function, location, and employment terms. Employees must follow the attendance system designated by the company.

topics.title: Attendance recording
topics.content: Employees must record attendance accurately. Proxy attendance, falsifying timesheets, sharing attendance credentials, or asking another person to record attendance on one's behalf is prohibited.

topics.title: Leave application
topics.content: Planned leave should normally be requested through the HR or attendance system before the leave begins. Emergency or unplanned absence should be communicated to the reporting manager as soon as reasonably possible.

topics.title: Remote and hybrid work
topics.content: Where remote or hybrid work is approved, employees remain responsible for working hours, availability, confidentiality, information security, and deliverables.

topics.title: Overtime and additional work
topics.content: Overtime, weekend work, or work on designated holidays must follow the approval process applicable to the employee's location and role.

manager_responsibilities: Set clear expectations for working hours and availability.
Approve or reject leave requests consistently and document exceptions.
Monitor workload and escalate recurring capacity issues.
Ensure attendance records are accurate and corrected through approved processes.

policies.title: Information Security and Data Protection

topics.title: Password and authentication
topics.content: Employees must use unique passwords for company accounts and must not share passwords or authentication codes. Multi-factor authentication must be enabled where required.

topics.title: Confidential information
topics.content: Confidential information includes customer information, employee records, candidate data, pricing, contracts, business plans, source code, credentials, technical specifications, quality records, and non-public financial information.

topics.title: Data classification
topics.content: Information should be treated according to its sensitivity. Public information may be shared externally when authorized. Internal information is intended for employees and approved partners. Confidential information requires controlled access. Highly restricted information requires explicit authorization and enhanced safeguards.

topics.title: Phishing and suspicious activity
topics.content: Employees must verify unexpected requests for passwords, payment changes, confidential files, or urgent transfers of information. Suspicious emails, links, attachments, login prompts, or unusual system behavior must be reported to Information Security promptly.

topics.title: Lost or stolen devices
topics.content: Loss or theft of a company device, access card, storage media, or mobile device containing company information must be reported immediately.

topics.title: AI and external tools
topics.content: Employees must not enter confidential, personal, customer, regulated, or proprietary information into public AI tools or external software unless the tool and use case have been approved by the company.

policies.security_rule: If you would not send the information to an unknown external recipient, do not paste it into an unapproved external service.

policies.title: Workplace Safety, Quality and Compliance

topics.title: Safety responsibilities
topics.content: Employees must follow site-specific safety procedures, use required personal protective equipment, maintain clear emergency routes, and report unsafe conditions.

topics.title: Incident and near-miss reporting
topics.content: Workplace injuries, environmental incidents, equipment damage, unsafe conditions, and near misses must be reported through the designated reporting process.

topics.title: Quality records
topics.content: Quality-related records must be accurate, complete, legible, attributable, and created at the time the activity is performed. Employees must not backdate records, destroy original evidence, or make undocumented changes to controlled records.

topics.title: Deviations and corrective actions
topics.content: A deviation is a departure from an approved procedure, specification, instruction, or expected condition. Employees must document deviations promptly and provide factual information for investigation.

topics.title: Training
topics.content: Employees must complete mandatory induction, compliance, safety, information security, and role-specific training within the assigned timelines.

topics.title: Audit cooperation
topics.content: Employees must provide accurate information during internal or external audits and must not conceal records or coach another person to provide misleading information.

policies.escalation_principle: When an employee identifies a potential safety, quality, regulatory, or data-integrity risk, the expected action is to stop or contain the affected activity where appropriate and escalate the issue through the defined process.

topics.title: Procurement
topics.content: Purchases must follow the approved procurement process. Employees must not split a purchase into smaller transactions to avoid approval thresholds.

topics.title: Supplier due diligence
topics.content: New suppliers may be subject to identity verification, tax documentation, banking verification, quality assessment, compliance screening, and other due-diligence checks.

topics.title: Business expenses
topics.content: Business expenses must be reasonable, necessary, supported by valid documentation, and submitted within the applicable claim period.

topics.title: Corporate cards
topics.content: Corporate cards are issued for authorized business expenditure only. Cardholders are responsible for safeguarding the card, reviewing transactions, submitting supporting documents, and reporting unauthorized transactions immediately.

topics.title: Company assets
topics.content: Laptops, mobile devices, equipment, furniture, access cards, software licenses, and other company assets must be protected from loss, misuse, unauthorized transfer, or damage.

policies.title: Travel, Communication and Social Media

topics.title: Business travel
topics.content: Business travel must be approved before booking unless an emergency exception applies. Employees should use approved travel channels and select reasonable options considering cost, safety, schedule, and business requirements.

topics.title: Travel expenses
topics.content: Eligible travel expenses may include transportation, accommodation, meals, local travel, and other approved business costs. Personal upgrades and expenses for accompanying family members are not reimbursable unless specifically approved.

topics.title: External communication
topics.content: Only authorized spokespersons may make official statements on behalf of the company.

topics.title: Social media
topics.content: Employees may use personal social-media accounts, but they must not disclose confidential information, publish customer or employee data without authorization, misrepresent personal opinions as official company statements, or misuse company trademarks.

topics.title: Recruitment and candidate information
topics.content: Candidate resumes, contact details, interview feedback, compensation information, and assessment records must be handled confidentially and only for legitimate recruitment purposes.

topics.title: Customer and partner communications
topics.content: Employees must provide accurate information to customers and partners. Commitments involving pricing, delivery timelines, contractual terms, regulatory claims, or technical specifications should be made only within the employee's authority.

communication_checklist: Is the information accurate and approved?
Does the recipient have a legitimate need to receive it?
Does the communication contain confidential or personal information?
Am I authorized to make this commitment or statement?
Would the communication create a legal, regulatory, security, or reputational risk?

policies.title: Grievance Handling, Reporting and Policy Administration

topics.title: Raising a concern
topics.content: Employees are encouraged to raise concerns promptly when they observe misconduct, safety risks, discrimination, harassment, fraud, conflicts of interest, data-security incidents, quality concerns, or other policy violations.

topics.title: Non-retaliation
topics.content: The company prohibits retaliation against a person who raises a concern in good faith or participates honestly in an investigation.

topics.title: Investigation process
topics.content: Reported concerns may be reviewed to determine whether an investigation is required. Investigations may involve interviews, document review, system records, and other appropriate evidence.

topics.title: Corrective action
topics.content: Where a policy violation is substantiated, the company may take corrective action consistent with the seriousness of the matter, applicable law, employment terms, and internal procedures.

topics.title: Policy exceptions
topics.content: Exceptions to this manual require documented approval from the policy owner or the authority specified in the relevant procedure.

topics.title: Policy review and ownership
topics.content: Human Resources and Corporate Compliance are responsible for coordinating periodic review of this manual.
